correctness.rationale: For every retained facet supported on a k-set, projection to the tangent hyperplane gives normal norm \(\sqrt{k(n-k)/n}\), while the common barycenter has slack \(k(n-k)/2\); hence its facet distance is \(\tfrac12\sqrt{nk(n-k)}\), minimized exactly at k=1 or n-1. For the permutahedron and associahedron, all singleton facets give an all-center upper bound that forces the uniform center at equality. For the parallelepiped, the parallel facets x_1=1 and x_1=n give the same sharp upper bound, and prefix/suffix inequalities give the full center box. All quantifiers and low-dimensional coincidences are handled explicitly.

value.rationale: The 2023 survey highlights the permutahedron, Loday associahedron, and Loday parallelepiped as a canonical nested trio and treats their common vertex barycenter as a surprising geometric property. The finding adds a second exact shared Euclidean invariant: all three have the same inradius and the same distinguished point is an incenter. It also shows that optimal-center geometry separates the trio, with uniqueness for the permutahedron and associahedron but an explicit positive-dimensional center family for the parallelepiped. This is a natural structural metric refinement of a well-established comparison, not an arbitrary slice or finite recomputation.
